valuation.method: Forward EPS x P/E (FY2027E diluted EPS viewed at the 12-month target date)

bear.driver: Macro slowdown, softer comp store sales, and freight/tariff cost pressure

base.driver: Steady mid-single-digit comp growth, stable merchandise margins, and ongoing share repurchases (~319.5M diluted shares)

bull.driver: Sustained high-single-digit comps, operating leverage, and off-price market share gains

valuation.implied_by_close: At base FY2027E EPS of $8.75, the $231.68 close implies 26.5x P/E; the $278.00 equal-weight post-Q2 named target implies 31.8x P/E or $9.93 EPS at 28.0x.
valuation.sensitivity: One turn of P/E moves the base target by $8.75 (3.8 pp of price return).
valuation.watch_metric: Comparable store sales growth and merchandise margin ex-tariff-refunds

analyst_notes: Following Ross Stores' Q2 FY2026 earnings beat on August 20, 2026 (EPS $2.66 including ~$0.60/sh one-time IEEPA tariff refund; FY2026 guidance raised to $8.61-$8.77), Evercore ISI (Michael Binetti) raised its target to $276 from $265 and Telsey Advisory Group (Dana Telsey) raised its target to $280 from $265, both maintaining Outperform. Broad Street consensus prior to Q3 sat around $270-$279, above our $245.00 base case, reflecting higher assumed FY2027E earnings or a ~31-32x multiple versus our 28.0x base multiple.
